title: The Radio City check he gave to his mother
summary: His valet tipped off Nazarro about the check, so Bubbles had his mother collect the $950 check, to Nazarro's fury.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: However, I got this partnership and we come to find out this boy that I had, this valet, he stole a briefcase I had in the car with these things in it and that's when my partner went and signed up an extra year with Nazarro when I had already fixed it so that I'm going to get -- see, when we were playing in Radio City Music Hall, I can go get the check because nobody knows I can't get the check but Nazarro. I can go get the check 'cause I'm part of the act and the leader of the act. So I go out and get the check cause I tell this boy

that I'm going to get the check. He goes and tells Nazarro. Nazarro comes and gets the check. That blocks that. They don't know that I've got this in my head to do, but I've got to do this with the check. I'm not anxious to have the money. I want to do something with the money that's necessary to do with it. I couldn't do it with pennies or nickels or dimes, I've got to do it with the sum of money that's necessary, you know.

So I figured the check would be necessary for me to do this with, to establish the name of Buck and Bubbles with this check -- account with this check. So would you believe that I got the check, he told on me this time but the next week he don't know I'm going to get the check and I didn't tell the valet. So I go get the check. So when he come to get the check -- now, my sister is passed now and my mother has gone to San Diego to bury my sister and get the children. This business happened about the check money while they're

there. So when I get the money, the check, Nazarro comes over to get the check and they told him John Bubbles got the check. He come back to me to give it to him. I ain't got the check because by this time my mother is back and I have my mother to come down to the theater and get the check. Mama comes to the theater, Radio City Music Hall back stage and I give my mother the check so I wouldn't be -- 'cause I'll go mad and just throw the whole thing in the jug house, you know. So I give my mother the check that's made out to Buck and Bubbles for the amount of salary we got there, okay? Only $950, that wasn't nothing.

But anyhow, she got the check. So I sent her back uptown with this check, back on 54th Street. She goes back with the check, when Nazarro comes over to the theater to get the money my mother done got the check going home, I tell him I ain't got it. I don't tell him where it is, I ain't got it.
"What did you do with the money?"

"I don't know, I must have spent it." He don't know where that check -- that it existed. The only idea about it was that he can't think of stopping the check because -- stopping a check to somebody it's paid to -- he can't do that. He couldn't have the people stop the check because they give it to me. That was sure bad management. Something was wrong somewhere. He don't want to show that.
